propositions: Push non-fast-forward recovery's merge abort path fails permanently when an untracked local file collides with a file the remote merge wants to create (e.g. *-SNAPSHOT.json, *.retired), leaving the store wedged across retries.

The recovery stash creates a commit object but clears only tracked changes via git reset --hard, deliberately leaving untracked files; merge abort then restores the stash without self-healing the collision.

The fix extends _recover_dirty_merge to parse abort-named untracked colliding paths using sync's shared parser, quarantine-move them to <git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/, and retry the merge exactly once before restoring the stash.

Stash restore ordering is preserved: quarantine and retry occur between the failed merge and stash restore, ensuring the stash commit is restored exactly once on every exit path (success, retry-failure, non-recoverable abort).

Genuine content conflicts and non-collision paths keep today's behavior unchanged; the mover fences all named paths on git status --porcelain -uall '??' before moving anything to prevent mis-parsing from relocating tracked data.
